    13	``towncrier`` is a utility to produce useful, summarised news files for your project.
    14	Rather than reading the Git history as some newer tools to produce it, or having one single file which developers all write to, ``towncrier`` reads "news fragments" which contain information `useful to end users`.
    15	
    16	
    17	Philosophy
    18	----------
    19	
    20	``towncrier`` delivers the news which is convenient to those that hear it, not those that write it.
    21	
    22	That is, by duplicating what has changed from the "developer log" (which may contain complex information about the original issue, how it was fixed, who authored the fix, and who reviewed the fix) into a "news fragment" (a small file containing just enough information to be useful to end users), ``towncrier`` can produce a digest of the changes which is valuable to those who may wish to use the software.
    23	These fragments are also commonly called "topfiles" or "newsfiles" in Twisted parlance.
    24	
    25	``towncrier`` works best in a development system where all merges involve closing a ticket.
    26	
    27	
    28	Quick Start
    29	-----------
    30	
    31	Install from PyPI::
    32	
    33	    python3 -m pip install towncrier
    34	
    35	.. note::
    36	
    37	   ``towncrier``, as a command line tool, works on Python 3.5+ only.
    38	   It is usable by projects written in other languages, provided you specify the project version either in the configuration file or on the command line.
    39	   For Python 2/3 compatible projects, the version can be discovered automatically.
    40	
    41	In your project root, add a ``towncrier.toml`` or a ``pyproject.toml`` file (if both files exist, the first will take precedence).
    42	You can configure your project in two ways.
    43	To configure it via an explicit directory, add:
    44	
    45	.. code-block:: ini
    46	
    47	    [tool.towncrier]
    48	    directory = "changes"
    49	
    50	Alternatively, to configure it relative to a (Python) package directory, add:
    51	
    52	.. code-block:: ini
    53	
    54	    [tool.towncrier]
    55	    package = "mypackage"
    56	    package_dir = "src"
    57	    filename = "NEWS.rst"

    59	For the latter, news fragments (see "News Fragments" below) should be in a ``newsfragments`` directory under your package.

    61	
    62	.. tip::
    63	
    64	    To prevent git from removing the ``newsfragments`` directory, make a ``.gitignore`` file in it with::
    65	
    66	        !.gitignore
    67	
    68	    This will keep the folder around, but otherwise "empty".
    69	
    70	``towncrier`` needs to know what version your project is, and there are three ways you can give it:
    71	
    72	- For Python 2/3 compatible projects, a ``__version__`` in the top level package.
    73	  This can be either a string literal, a tuple, or an `Incremental <https://github.com/hawkowl/incremental>`_ version.
    74	
    75	- Manually passing ``--version=<myversionhere>`` when interacting with ``towncrier``.

- **Problem**: When running `towncrier --draft` for the first time, if the newsfragments directory doesn't exist, it crashes with an unhandled `FileNotFoundError` traceback

2. **Catching `OSError`** (which includes `FileNotFoundError`) 
3. **Automatically creating the missing directory** using `os.makedirs(section_dir)`
4. **Continuing with an empty file list** (`files = []`)

```python
try:
    files = os.listdir(section_dir)

    os.makedirs(section_dir)
```
